one_line_contribution: An intervention-anchored audit of learned per-item memory utilities: co-retrieval with a planted wrong-procedure item is randomised as a dose across a 120-item bystander class, and each scorer family (outcome Q, MemQ TD(lambda), RoMeRL coordinates, flag-oracle, LOO-corrected Q) is judged by how far its Spearman with forced-retrieval leave-one-out ground truth collapses as dose rises, plus the measured LLM-call cost of the de-pooling fix.
closest_prior_work: RoMeRL, arXiv:2608.02508 (VERIFIED via s2cli channel (a), S2 record 2026-08-03, HF record 2026-08-10). Its own abstract states that 'because trajectory-level rewards are jointly assigned to co-retrieved memories, irrelevant experiences may receive misleading utility updates and consequently enter the memory-reward trap', and that reduced-order utility states 'limit persistent reward contamination'. So the phenomenon, its name, its causal story and a proposed remedy are all already published; what is left new here is the measurement — a randomised co-retrieval dose and a rank correlation against forced-retrieval LOO, which RoMeRL indeed never runs (it reports downstream success only). That caps rather than kills novelty: this is an audit paper of another paper's premise, and it is doubly exposed because the RoMeRL scorer under test is reconstructed from that abstract, so P2's 'published remedy fails' result is a claim about the reviewers' reconstruction, not the released method. Secondary threats, both verified and both non-fatal: CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467 (2026-04-07, S2) is the intervention-based per-item utility measurement but only for single-shot RAG with no learned utility to validate; MemQ arXiv:2605.08374 (2026-05-08/12, S2+HF, cit 2) is the DAG-credit target and again never checks an item against removal; Memory-R2 arXiv:2605.21768 and CHIME arXiv:2609.02074 (2026-09-02) are credit-aware training/write-time policies with no counterfactual item check. Data Shapley arXiv:1904.02868 (verified) is the home ancestor and supplies the noise-of-per-datum-values warning the proposal correctly inherits.
strongest_objection: The entire quantitative apparatus is a ladder of differences of Spearman correlations built on a baseline the proposal itself only requires to clear 0.25. E0(b) admits the study if Spearman(pass-A Q, clean LOO) >= 0.25 over 60 items; P1 then demands that this same baseline drop by >= 0.20; P2 partitions that 0.20 into '<= 25% recovered' versus '>= 75% recovered' bands, i.e. 0.05-wide bands, against a stated per-correlation SE of ~0.08 and a difference-of-dependent-correlations SE that is not smaller. A study that passes its own gate at 0.28 and reports a 0.22 drop has a mixed-pass correlation of ~0.06 and cannot separate any of P2's or P3's claims from zero — exactly the outcome the automated entailment check reaches independently by marking P2 and P3 unresolvable. Compounding it, the LOO 'ground truth' is a 48-pair per-item estimate with SE ~0.10 whose split-half reliability the proposal concedes may sit below 0.5, so both terms of every correlation are near their own noise floor, and disattenuation by an unreliable reliability estimate will produce corrected values with CIs spanning the whole admissible range. Two concrete design faults make this worse rather than merely uncertain. (i) The flag-oracle, billed as the 'reachable upper bound' that anchors P2 and voids it if it recovers <50%, updates B only from episodes without a W item — but dose-1 items have W in every one of their 24 scheduled episodes, so 40 of 120 items receive no oracle update at all and their oracle Q is empty or built from a handful of unscheduled stream retrievals. The upper bound is undefined for a third of the class, which mechanically depresses the oracle and triggers P2's own void clause. (ii) The 100% corrected-Q ceiling that both falsifying branches of P3 hinge on is computed on 40 items (Spearman SE ~0.165) and compared against a 120-item pass-A correlation on a different item set; the 0.05 and 0.10 margins are inside that ceiling's own noise. Finally there is a circularity the proposal names but does not resolve: P1, P3 and P5 treat single-removal REPLACE-static3 LOO as ground truth while P4 is a test that single-removal LOO is a biased estimator; if P4 confirms non-additivity at <= -10 net, the anchor of the headline result is itself known to be wrong, and the paper has no second anchor.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Re-anchor P2 and P3 on the observed drop rather than the pre-registered one: score them only if the measured P1 drop exceeds a pre-registered floor (0.35 or so), and derive each scorer-difference MDE from a paired item-level bootstrap of the scorer difference estimated empirically from A vs A', not inherited from the A-vs-M SE. 2) Fix the flag-oracle by replacing the {0, 0.5, 1} dose grid with {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75} or by holding out 6 of the 24 scheduled episodes as guaranteed W-free for every item, so the upper bound is estimable at every dose. 3) Run every term of P3 — pass A, M1, 20%, 100% — on the identical 40-item subset so the ceiling comparison is paired. 4) Raise the entry gate: require pass-A Spearman(Q, LOO) >= 0.45, not 0.25, or state up front that the headline is reported as a proportional loss of an explicitly weak baseline. 5) Resolve the P4 circularity by pre-committing to a decision rule: if class-mean interaction is <= -10 net, re-score P1/P3/P5 against pairwise-removal or a small exact-Shapley ground truth on a subset, and report the headline under both anchors. 6) Report the per-item LOO split-half reliability before scoring anything, and drop items below a threshold rather than disattenuating the whole class. 7) Report the dose-response as three separate Spearman values (dose 0, 0.5, 1 subgroups) plus the slope, not only the pooled mixed-versus-A contrast — a per-dose curve is the actual dose-response quantity the hypothesis names and is far more informative than one difference.
missing_baseline: A free offline de-pooling estimator fit to the same logs: least-squares / regression credit assignment on the retrieved-set design matrix (regress episode outcome on binary item-membership indicators over the pass's episodes, optionally ridge-penalised or with rank and task-type covariates), i.e. the standard shared-reward decomposition (linear value decomposition, Banzhaf/leverage-style estimators, or IPW-corrected Q using the logged planting propensity d, which is known by construction). This costs zero extra episodes and is precisely designed to separate co-occurring contributors from a shared outcome. Its absence is fatal to the paper's economic claim: the proposal concludes that de-pooling requires either an oracle flag or a paid LOO-corrected Q at a measured LLM-call cost, but if a regression on the already-logged retrieval matrix recovers most of the drop for free, P3's 'costed fix' is the wrong headline. A reviewer will also ask for the propensity-weighted Q specifically, since the design randomises dose and therefore hands the estimator a known treatment probability. Secondary omissions: no random-pruning baseline for P5's decision-cost claim, and no scorer that simply subtracts the episode's set-mean outcome (a within-set centring control).
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is one of the better ones I have seen in this round — five classed queries, IDs and dates attached, channel reported (s2=ok hf=ok), two IDs explicitly verified, and it correctly identifies RoMeRL as its own nearest neighbour rather than hiding it. Two defects in it: arXiv:2605.30712 is cited as 'ExpSuite' with 'with/without-set feedback' but the record returned by channel (a) is 'ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents' — a mis-citation carried into the Related Work; and arXiv:2507.04480 ('document Shapley'), one of the two ground-truth-side anchors, is NOT FOUND on either Semantic Scholar or HuggingFace, so I could not verify it and the proposal should not lean on it. My own searches, all via channel (a) s2cli.py (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace), all answered s2=ok hf=ok; WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is prohibited, so no query fell through to channel (b). Q1 [mechanism, --recent] 'co-retrieval reward contamination per-item memory utility leave-one-out ground truth LLM agent' -> 12 hits: RoMeRL 2608.02508, Memory Reward Inflation 2608.00017 (self-graded reward inflation / Echo Gap, a different failure), Memory-R2 2605.21768, TreeMem 2605.04811, InfoMem 2606.03329, MemSifter 2603.03379, plus off-topic RLVR/reward-hacking items; none measures a learned item utility against removal. Q2 [mechanism, all time] 'validating learned memory item utility scores against counterfactual removal rank correlation' -> 12 hits, only CUE-R 2604.05467 on target and it is single-shot RAG with no learned score; the rest are counterfactual work in vision, ranking and recommendation. Q3 [closest named method] 'MemQ provenance DAG TD-lambda credit propagation memory item Q-value agent' -> 10 hits, MemQ 2605.08374 confirmed (s2+hf, cit 2), plus CMI-Mem 2607.20553, Mem-T 2601.23014, D-MEM 2603.14597, MemFactory 2603.29493; none validates its Q against an intervention. Q4 [mechanism variant, --recent] 'shared outcome reward co-occurring items credit misattribution dose manipulation valuation rank scramble' -> 6 hits (2511.10687 credit-conserving multi-agent signals, SCPO 2605.09287-adjacent step credit, PiCA 2605.09287); nothing on stored-item utilities. Q5 [home literature, no agent/memory words] 'data valuation ground truth leave-one-out rank correlation evaluating value estimators correlated points' -> 10 hits: Data Shapley 1904.02868 (verified), joint Shapley 2107.11357, For-Value 2508.10180, DVGS 2405.08217; the sample-cost and rank-instability warnings are real prior art the proposal already cites, but none concerns shared-reward contamination of a learned score. Q6 [adjacent threat, --recent] 'planted corrupted memory entry contaminates utility of co-retrieved benign entries agent memory poisoning pruning' -> 9 hits: MemoryGraft 2512.16962, Zombie Agents 2602.15654, Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense 2601.05504, SuperLocalMemory 2603.02240 — the planting manipulation exists in the security literature but always as an attack on behaviour, never as a randomised dose used to audit a utility estimator, so no collision. IDs I verified via channel (a): 2608.02508 (RoMeRL), 2605.08374 (MemQ), 2306.07929 (REMEMBERER, indexed under 'Large Language Models Are Semi-Parametric Reinforcement Learning Agents'), 2601.03192 (MemRL, cit 85), 2605.21768 (Memory-R2), 2609.02074 (CHIME, 2026-09-02), 2606.29502 (UCOB), 2604.05467 (CUE-R), 1904.02868 (Data Shapley). IDs I could NOT verify: 2507.04480 (returned not found); 2605.30712 verified but under a different title/method than the proposal claims. Net: the novelty argument survives the search, but it survives at the level the search establishes — nobody has run this measurement, while the phenomenon it measures is already asserted, named and 'addressed' in a verified August 2026 preprint.
